deities: Durga/Shakti (worshipped in the form of a giant trishul)

history.period: Ancient (mentioned in the Skanda Purana's Kedar Khanda); age of the trishul variously estimated over 1500 years (weakly sourced, unverified)
history.summary: Prominent Shakti shrine within the Vishwanath temple complex, opposite the Vishwanath shrine on the Bhagirathi bank. Its centrepiece is a 6-metre iron-and-copper trident believed to be Durga's weapon against demons; local belief says it cannot be moved by force but vibrates at a gentle touch. Legends include a failed Gorkha-period excavation attempt and Tibetan/Naga-dynasty inscriptions on the trident - all unverified. OVERLAP NOTE: this temple stands in the same complex as the Vishwanath Temple (row 4, id vishwanath-temple-uttarkashi); consider whether the CSV's two rows should be kept separate or merged. CSV town Uttarkashi is correct; CSV 'state' column holds town names - corrected to Uttarakhand.

name: Shakti Temple
town_description: Uttarkashi is a pilgrim town in the Garhwal Himalaya on the Bhagirathi river, the district headquarters and a key Char Dham stopover en route to Gangotri.

travel.road: In the main town of Uttarkashi, about 1 km from the bus stand, inside the Vishwanath temple complex.

visitor_information.best_time: March to May and September to November; Navratri and Dussehra draw the largest crowds.
visitor_information.opening_hours: 5 AM to 1 PM and 4 PM to 8 PM (verify before visiting).
